title: Holi Festival Event Outfit: Colour Run Style Guide for 2027
excerpt: What to wear to a ticketed Holi festival or colour run abroad: breathable cotton, smart layers, the right shoes and a simple carry list.
body:
For a ticketed Holi festival or colour run, wear a loose cotton tunic or kurta with leggings or palazzos, a light layer you can tie around your waist, and closed trainers you are happy to stain. Choose breathable cotton over synthetics, carry a small cross-body bag, and leave anything precious at home.

This guide is for anyone heading to an outdoor Holi event in the UK, USA, Canada or Australia, where you may queue, run, dance and stand on grass for hours. A simple [sky blue hand block print cotton tunic top](/products/sky-blue-hand-block-print-cotton-tunic-top/) at $27 is an easy place to start.

## What should you wear to a Holi colour run?

Colour runs are about movement. You walk or jog a set route, get dusted at colour stations and finish with a crowd party. That means fabric that stays light when dusty, a length that does not tangle around your knees, and nothing that needs constant adjusting.

A hip-length or thigh-length cotton tunic over leggings or joggers is the easiest answer. It covers you when you bend, lets air move, and the print hides patches of colour so you still look put together in photos at the finish line. Skip floor-length kurtas and flowing dupattas for the run itself, because they catch underfoot and drag through wet powder.

If the event is more festival than run, with music stages, food stalls and long stretches of standing, you can go a little more festive. A kurta palazzo set gives you the Holi look without giving up comfort.

## Is a kurta set or a co-ord better for an outdoor Holi festival?

Both work. The right one depends on how active your day will be, so use this quick guide.

| Event type | Best outfit | Layer | Footwear |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colour run or fun run | Cotton tunic with leggings or joggers | Light zip hoodie tied at the waist | Old running trainers |
| Day festival with music stages | Cotton kurta palazzo set | Denim or cotton jacket | Closed canvas trainers |
| Family park event | Printed co-ord set | Cardigan or shacket | Slip-on trainers with grip |
| Evening after-party | A fresh second outfit kept in your bag | Shawl or long jacket | Clean flats |

For a festival day, the [sage teal hand block print cotton kurta palazzo set](/products/sage-teal-block-print-cotton-kurta-palazzo-set/) is a strong pick. Palazzos give you room to dance, and teal is a base colour that makes pink and yellow gulal look bright rather than muddy.

If you prefer something less traditional, a printed co-ord feels relaxed and modern. The [white and blue floral cotton halter peplum top with palazzo co-ord set](/products/white-blue-floral-cotton-halter-peplum-top-with-palazzo-co-ord-set/) suits warmer events in Australia or a sunny spring day elsewhere, with a light shirt thrown over it if the morning starts cool.

## How should you layer for a spring Holi event abroad?

Holi falls in late March 2027 (check your local calendar). That is early spring in the UK, USA and Canada and early autumn in Australia. Mornings can be chilly and afternoons mild, and the weather feels very different once you are damp with coloured water.

Think in three thin layers rather than one thick one. Start with a fitted cotton or thermal base if it is cold, add your tunic or kurta, then finish with a jacket you do not mind ruining. An old denim jacket is ideal because coloured powder looks almost intentional on it. When the sun comes out, tie it around your waist and keep dancing.

Avoid wool coats and anything that is dry-clean only. Colour settles into the fibres, and you will spend the next week trying to rescue it.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Hand block printed cotton is the fabric we would choose for a day like this. It is soft, it breathes while you move, and a multi-colour print already has the busy, layered look that colour play creates, so splashes blend in rather than stand out. Wash it separately in cold water for the first few washes.

## What shoes are best for a Holi festival or colour run?

Shoes matter more than most people expect. By the afternoon the ground at outdoor events is often grass, mud or wet tarmac, and coloured water soaks straight through mesh.

- **Closed trainers you will retire afterwards:** old running shoes are perfect for a colour run.
- **Dark socks:** white socks turn pink within minutes.
- **Grip over style:** wet powder on grass is slippery.
- **No sandals or open toes:** crowded, wet ground is a bad mix with bare feet.
- **A spare pair in your bag:** for the trip home, so your car or train seat stays clean.

## What should you carry to a ticketed Holi event?

Keep it small and hands-free. A cross-body or belt bag sits close to your body and is easy to keep an eye on in a crowd. Put your phone in a zip pouch or waterproof sleeve, and carry one card plus the ticket on your phone.

Also pack a plastic bag for wet clothes, a small towel, wipes, a hair tie and a fresh top for the ride home. One note on etiquette: play only with people who are clearly joining in, and always ask before you colour someone's face.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should I wear to a Holi colour run?**
A loose cotton tunic over leggings or joggers, a light jacket you can tie at your waist, and old closed trainers. Leave long dupattas and floor-length hems for another day.

**Do I have to wear white to a Holi festival event?**
No. White shows colour beautifully, but a printed or pastel cotton outfit hides stains, photographs well and is easier to wear again afterwards.

**Can I wear jeans to a Holi colour run?**
You can, but denim gets heavy and cold once it is soaked. Leggings, joggers or cotton palazzos stay lighter and dry faster.

**How do I wash Holi colour out of a cotton kurta?**
Shake off dry powder outdoors first, then rinse in cold water and wash the piece separately. Avoid hot water at the start, as it can help colour settle into the fabric.
